jina: Provisions relating to offices established by this Constitution
maudhui: (1) Any person holding an office established by this Constitution (including the office of Minister, Deputy Minister or Member of Parliament, except an ex officio Member of Parliament) may resign by giving notice in writing signed by him, in accordance with the following procedure— (a) if such person was appointed or elected by one person, then such notice of resignation shall be submitted to the person who appointed or elected him, or if he was appointed or elected by a body of persons, then such notice of resignation shall be submitted to that body; (b) if such person is the President, then the notice of resignation shall be submitted to the Speaker; (c) if such person is the Speaker or Deputy Speaker, then the notice of resignation shall be submitted to the National Assembly; and (d) if such person is a Member of Parliament, then the notice of resignation shall be submitted to the Speaker. (2) A person who has given notice of resignation in accordance with the provisions of subarticle (1) of this Article shall be deemed to have resigned from the day on which the notice of resignation is received by the person or body concerned, or by a person authorized to receive such notice, but if the notice of resignation states that the person concerned will resign from a date later than the date on which the notice is received, then such person shall be deemed to have resigned from that later date. (3) Where a person holding an office established by this Constitution resigns, then if he has all the qualifications and is in every respect eligible, he may be appointed or elected again to hold that office in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution. (4) The provisions of subarticle (3) of this Article shall not prevent a person who is President from being re-elected President while he is still holding the office of President.
